Factoring Trinomials (a ≠ 1): Two More Methods Algebra 3/4 · Notes p. 68–69

Algebra 3/4 · Factoring

Factoring Trinomials (a ≠ 1): Two More Methods

Bottoms Up (slide and divide) and Guess-and-Check. Have your notebook open to pages 68–69.

2x2 + 5x + 3  ⟶  (x + 1)(2x + 3)

Page 68 · Method 2: Bottoms Up (AKA Slide and Divide)

• This shortcut helps you temporarily get rid of a

1. FACTOR GCF FIRST

2. Multiply your a and c

a. Replace c with a · c

3. Find two numbers that multiply to ac and add to b.

a. Use AC/"X" method/grouping

b. Write as (x + ___)(x + ___)

4. Divide both constants by a.

a. Reduce the fraction

5. Bring any remaining denominator to the front of the x.

Page 68 · Example 1 · Factor completely

2x2 + 5x + 3

x² + 5x + 6 ← 2 · 3 = 6
(x + 2)(x + 3)
(x + 22)(x + 32)
(x + 1)(x + 32)
(x + 1)(2x + 3)
6235
factors of 61 + 6 = 72 + 3 = 5

Page 69 · Method 3: Guess-and-Check

• For those who want to brute force it

1. FACTOR GCF FIRST

2. Determine your factors' signs

3. List the factor pairs of a and factor pairs of c

4. Guess: Place a pair in the front spots and a pair in the back spots

5. Check:

a. outer + inner = b ?

i. If not, swap the back numbers or try a new pair

Page 69 · Example 1 · Factor completely

3x2 + 11x − 20

c − → opposite signs · b + → larger is positive

Factors of 3: 1 × 3 Factors of −20: −1 × 20, −2 × 10, −4 × 5
Guess 1(3x − 2)(x + 10)Out: (3x)(10) = 30xIn: (−2)(x) = −2x→ 28x ✗
Guess 2(3x + 10)(x − 2)Out: (3x)(−2) = −6xIn: (10)(x) = 10x→ 4x ✗
Guess 3(3x − 4)(x + 5)Out: (3x)(5) = 15xIn: (−4)(x) = −4x→ 11x ✓
(3x − 4)(x + 5)

Review

Four things to watch for

1

GCF first, no matter which method you use.

2

Slide and divide: don't forget to divide by a, and bring any leftover denominator to the front of the x.

3

Guess and check: use the signs first. It cuts down how many guesses you need.

4

Check. Multiply your answer back out. It should match the problem.

Wrap-up

Three ways to factor when a ≠ 1

  1. The X method: a · c on top, b on the bottom, then group.
  2. Bottoms up: slide a onto c, factor, divide by a, bring the denominator to the front.
  3. Guess-and-check: pick the signs, guess, and check outer + inner = b. done

Use whichever one makes sense to you. They all give the same answer.

Optional

Practice on your own

Six problems. Use any method you like. For each one:

  1. Work it in your notebook. GCF first!
  2. Stuck? Hint 1 gets you started. Hint 2 shows the two numbers.
  3. Pick your answer to check it. Wrong answers tell you what to fix.

Practice 1 of 6 Optional

Factor completely: 2x2 + 7x + 3

Hint 1 · What goes on the X

Slide: x² + 7x + 6. Find two numbers that multiply to 6 and add to 7.

Hint 2 · The two factors

The two factors are 1 and 6 → (x + 1/2)(x + 6/2).

Solution
(2x + 1)(x + 3)

Practice 2 of 6 Optional

Factor completely: 3x2 − 10x + 8

Hint 1 · What goes on the X

Slide: x² − 10x + 24. c is positive and b is negative, so both numbers are negative.

Hint 2 · The two factors

The two factors are −4 and −6 → (x − 4/3)(x − 6/3).

Solution
(3x − 4)(x − 2)

Practice 3 of 6 Optional

Factor completely: 5x2 + 9x − 2

Hint 1 · What goes on the X

Slide: x² + 9x − 10. c is negative and b is positive, so the larger number is positive.

Hint 2 · The two factors

The two factors are 10 and −1 → (x + 10/5)(x − 1/5).

Solution
(5x − 1)(x + 2)

Practice 4 of 6 Optional

Factor completely: 2x2 − x − 6

Hint 1 · What goes on the X

Guess-and-check: factors of 2 are 1 × 2. Factors of −6: 1 × −6, −1 × 6, 2 × −3, −2 × 3. c is negative, so the signs are opposite.

Hint 2 · The two factors

The two factors are 3 and −2 in the back spots.

Solution
(2x + 3)(x − 2)

Practice 5 of 6 Optional

Factor completely: 6x2 + 5x − 4

Hint 1 · What goes on the X

a · c = 6 · (−4) = −24. Find two numbers that multiply to −24 and add to 5.

Hint 2 · The two factors

The two factors are 8 and −3.

Solution
(3x + 4)(2x − 1)

Practice 6 of 6 Optional

Factor completely: 4x2 + 2x − 6

Hint 1 · What goes on the X

GCF first: 2(2x² + x − 3). Then factor 2x² + x − 3.

Hint 2 · The two factors

The two factors are 3 and −2 (a · c = −6, b = 1).

Solution
2(2x + 3)(x − 1)
